# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN SAUL

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Old Doctor Dave” together with “Mrs. Doctor Dave” had traveled down to the small dwelling so that they could welcome the husband and wife. Doctor Dave was a large, merry, white-bearded aged man, whereas Mrs. Doctor was a neat, pink-cheeked, gray-haired small woman who immediately embraced Nell, both in reality and in spirit.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0000 }

“My dear, seeing you brings me such joy. It must be that you are truly exhausted. A little evening meal is waiting for us, and some trout was carried up for you by Captain Saul. Where have you gone, Captain Saul? Ah, my guess is that he stepped outside to tend to the horse. Let us go to the upper floor so you can remove your coat.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0001 }

Bright, appreciative eyes glanced around Nell as she went up the stairs behind Mrs. Doctor Dave. The look of her new dwelling pleased her immensely. It appeared to possess Grey Shutters' atmosphere alongside the flavor belonging to her old traditions.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0002 }

“It seems to me that Miss Elizabeth Russell and I would have been 'kindred spirits,'” she whispered once she was by herself in her room. Two windows were located inside it; the one in the dormer faced the lower harbor, the sand-bar, and the Seven Gulls lighthouse.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0003 }

“A magical window giving onto the spray Of dangerous oceans in desolate realm of fays,”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0004 }

recited Nell in a low voice. Looking out the gable window, one could see a small, harvest-colored valley intersected by a brook. Located a half-mile up this brook stood the solitary visible dwelling—an ancient, sprawling, gray structure encircled by enormous willows, with its windows peering through them into the dusk like timid, searching eyes. Nell pondered who resided there; as her closest neighbors, she hoped they would be pleasant. All at once, her thoughts turned to the lovely girl with the white geese.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0005 }

“Hugh believed she was out of place here,” Nell reflected, “yet I am certain she fits. She possessed a quality that connected her to the ocean, the sky, and the port. Seven Gulls flows through her veins.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0006 }

As Nell reached the bottom of the stairs, Hugh stood in front of the fireplace, engaged in conversation with a man she did not know. Upon Nell’s entrance, both men turned toward her.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0007 }

“Nell, meet Captain Garrick. Captain Garrick, I’d like you to meet my wife.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0008 }

Never before had Hugh spoken the words “my wife” to anyone except Nell, and the sheer pride of doing so almost made him burst. Extending a muscular hand toward Nell, the old captain exchanged smiles with her, establishing a friendship between them right then. One like-minded soul instantly recognized another.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0009 }

“I am truly delighted to make your acquaintance, Mistress Carrow; and my wish is that your happiness equals that of the initial bride who arrived at this place. No finer wish could I offer you than THAT. However, the introduction given by your husband is not quite precise. My weekday title is 'Captain Saul' and, since you are bound to finish by using it, you may as well start by calling me that. You are undoubtedly a lovely little bride, Mistress Carrow. Gazing at you gives me a feeling as though I have only just gotten wedded myself.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0010 }

As the laughter died down, Mrs. Doctor Dave pressed Captain Saul to remain and join them for supper.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0011 }

“I am very grateful to you. It will be a true pleasure, Mistress Doctor. Generally, I must consume my food by myself, accompanied only by the image of my hideous aged visage in an opposing mirror. I rarely get the opportunity to share a meal with a pair of such delightful, attractive women.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0012 }

The praise from Captain Saul might appear quite plain when written down, yet his delivery possessed a manner and expression of such polite, tender respect that the lady receiving it perceived she was receiving a royal homage in a grand manner.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0013 }

An old man of high soul and simple mind, Captain Saul possessed everlasting youth within his heart and eyes. His tall and somewhat awkward form leaned forward slightly, but it still implied immense endurance and power; his hair was an iron-gray, thick mane that hung down to his shoulders, while his closely shaved face was bronzed and heavily furrowed; and his deep-set, exceptionally blue eyes would occasionally twinkle, occasionally dream, and at times gaze out toward the sea with a yearning search, like somebody hunting for a lost, precious object. Nell would discover on a future day the exact thing that Captain Saul was seeking.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0014 }

Captain Saul was undeniably a plain-looking man. Beauty had not guided the shaping of his thin jaws, rough mouth, and broad forehead; furthermore, his frame and his inner self bore the visible scars of numerous trials and griefs he had endured; yet despite Nell initially viewing him as unattractive, she gave the matter no further thought, because his rough exterior was so completely illuminated and transformed by the light of his soul.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0015 }

Cheerful spirits marked their assembly surrounding the evening meal table. Although the chill belonging to the September dusk was expelled by the hearth fire, sea gusts came in as they pleased through the unclosed dining room window. Encompassing the harbor alongside the expanse of muted, purple heights past it, the vista was splendid. Delights prepared by Mrs. Doctor piled the table, yet the large plate of sea trout served undeniably as the main attraction.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0016 }

“I imagined they would be rather delicious following a journey,” Captain Saul remarked. “Mistress Carrow, these trout are as fresh as possible. A couple of hours back, the Glen Pond was where they were swimming.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0017 }

“Who is looking after the beacon this evening, Captain Saul?” Doctor Dave inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0018 }

“Nephew Hector. His understanding of it matches my own. Well, now, I am truly pleased that you invited me to remain for supper. My hunger is quite strong—I ate very little for dinner today.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0019 }

“I reckon you are nearly starving yourself much of the duration down at that lighthouse,” Mrs. Doctor Dave stated sternly. “You refuse to take the effort to cook a proper meal.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0020 }

“Oh, Mistress Doctor, indeed I do,” Captain Saul asserted. “Listen, my usual way of living is royal. Up at the Glen yesterday evening, two pounds of steak were bought by me to bring back. Today, my intention was to enjoy an extraordinarily fine dinner.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0021 }

“And the steak, what became of it?” Mrs. Doctor Dave inquired. “Was it lost by you on your journey back?”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0022 }

“No.” Captain Saul appeared embarrassed. “Right at bedtime a pitiful, mean-tempered kind of dog showed up and requested a place to stay for the night. I suppose he was owned by one of the fishermen along the shore. I was unable to send the poor mongrel away—his foot was hurt. Consequently, I locked him inside the porch, gave him an old bag for a bed, and retired for the night. However, for some reason I was unable to rest. Upon reflecting on it, I somewhat recalled that the dog appeared starved.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0023 }

“And you arose and presented him with that steak—EVERY BIT OF that steak,” Mrs. Doctor Dave stated, expressing a sort of victorious scolding.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0024 }

“Indeed, no other food was available for him,” Captain Saul remarked apologetically. “At least, nothing that would appeal to a dog. He devoured it in roughly two mouthfuls, so I suppose he truly was famished. For the remainder of the night, my slumber was excellent, though my noon meal ended up rather meager—essentially just potatoes with nothing to accompany them. As for the dog, he dashed back toward his own place earlier today. I guess he had no desire to be a vegetarian.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0025 }

“Imagine going hungry over an good-for-nothing hound!” Mrs. Doctor scoffed.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0026 }

“Someone might consider him quite valuable, for all you know,” Captain Saul argued. “He failed to APPEAR to be worth much, yet a dog’s appearance can be deceiving. He could possess genuine inner beauty, just as I do. I must admit, the First Mate disapproved of him. His words were exceedingly harsh. Nevertheless, the First Mate holds a bias. A cat's view regarding a dog carries no weight. Regardless, I missed my meal, which makes this fine meal among this charming group truly enjoyable. Having wonderful neighbors is a wonderful blessing.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0027 }

“In the house nestled in the willows further up the brook, who resides there?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0028 }

“Mrs. Rufus Vane,” Captain Saul stated—“and her husband,” he appended, as though he were offering a subsequent thought.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0029 }

Nell beamed, forming an impression of Mrs. Rufus Vane based on how Captain Saul phrased it; clearly another Mrs. Agatha Sowerby.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0030 }

“You haven’t got a lot of neighbors, Mistress Carrow,” Captain Saul continued. “On this side of the harbor, the settlement is very sparse. A majority of the land is owned by Mr. Stroud up yonder past the Glen, and he leases it for pasture. Now, the opposite side of the harbor is crowded with people—MacAllisters in particular. There is an entire settlement of MacAllisters where if you throw a stone, you are bound to strike one. I had a conversation with old Leon Blacquiere recently. He has spent the whole summer working on the harbor. 'Dey’re nearly all MacAllisters over thar,’ he said to me. 'Dare’s Neil MacAllister and Sandy MacAllister and William MacAllister and Hector MacAllister and Angus MacAllister—and I believe dare’s de Devil MacAllister.’”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0031 }

“There are almost the same number of Kerrs and Crawfords,” Doctor Dave remarked, once the laughing had died down. “You see, Hugh, those of us living on this side of Seven Gulls share an ancient proverb—'From the conceit of the Kerrs, the pride of the MacAllisters, and the vainglory of the Crawfords, good Lord deliver us.’”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0032 }

“However, a good deal of splendid folks are in their midst,” Captain Saul stated. “I went to sea beside William Crawford across a long stretch of years, and when it came to bravery, stamina, and honesty, nobody was his peer. People possess intelligence across there beyond Seven Gulls. Perhaps that reason explains why the inhabitants here are somewhat disposed to hassle them. It is peculiar, is it not, the way people appear to begrudge anybody coming into the world just a bit sharper than themselves.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0033 }

Doctor Dave, having engaged in a forty-year dispute with the individuals from over the harbor, chuckled and quieted down.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0034 }

“What person resides in the bright emerald house roughly half a mile further along the road?” inquired Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0035 }

A pleased grin spread across the face of Captain Saul.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0036 }

“Miss Winifred Tolley. Because you are Presbyterians, she will probably come to visit you before long. She would not visit whatsoever if you happened to be Methodists. Methodists fill Winifred with a sacred dread.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0037 }

“She is quite a personality,” Doctor Dave laughed softly. “An exceptionally confirmed hater of men!”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0038 }

“Unripe fruit?” asked Hugh, chuckling.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0039 }

“No, ’tisn’t sour grapes,” replied Captain Saul in a serious manner. “Winifred had the ability to select anyone she wanted during her youth. Even now, the old widowers would jump the moment she uttered the word. It simply appears that she was born possessing a kind of persistent malice toward Methodists and men. Within Seven Gulls, hers is the most venomous tongue and the most compassionate heart. That woman turns up to assist in the gentlest manner whenever there is any difficulty. Another woman is never the subject of a cruel remark from her, and I suppose our thick old skins can endure it if she enjoys dressing down us poor scalawags of men.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0040 }

“Saul, Captain, she has only good things to say about you,” Mrs. Doctor remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0041 }

“Indeed, I fear that is the case. I really dislike it. It gives me the impression that there might be something rather unnatural concerning myself.”
{: #nw-v04-c06-p0042 }
